headline: House panel backs psychedelic care for veterans, with questions
pages: A US House Veterans Affairs subcommittee gave bipartisan backing Wednesday to psychedelic-assisted mental health treatment for veterans, while pressing Trump administration officials on readiness. Federal regulators could be close to approving such treatment. The Veterans Health Administration says just over 2 million veterans have treatment-resistant depression and about 180,000 would likely qualify for treatment with compounds including MDMA, psilocybin, LSD, DMT and ibogaine.

Lawmakers questioned officials for about two and a half hours on how the VA would deliver labor-intensive treatments if the Food and Drug Administration approves them, and whether federal law enforcement and health agencies are aligned. Nearly 6,500 veterans died by suicide in 2024, according to the VA's latest report. Subcommittee chair Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks, an Iowa Republican, said the numbers have remained stubbornly stagnant. If you need help in a crisis, call or text 988. Source: Idaho Capital Sun.
